newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady to weaker, fuel down.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady to weaker, fuel down.

text.p: Med oil products were steady to weaker on Thursday, traders said.
Naphtha held steady at a notional $202/$204 cif but traders said the market was tightening as supplies continued to be fixed for the Far East for early March.

Two cargoes totalling 115,000 tonnes were confirmed fixed out of Skikda for Japan. Another large cargo was rumoured to be sailing there as well, along with smaller Greek and Egyptian cargoes, but this was not confirmed.
Traders said the loss of at least 150,000 tonnes would support prices in the Med and that would spillover to NWE.
Gasoline was also steady with tight supply and recent demand from the eastern Med underpinning prices.
High sulphur fuel oil was sharply weaker as bunker demand sagged, and after Turkey's tenders to sell high sulphur fuel and buy low sulphur fuel.
Tupras tendered to buy 60-65,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil for delivery into Izmir and Izmit in late March, and dealers said they saw end user interest from Italy in the same period.
A Spanish refiner fixed a 30,000 tonne vessel to load in Scandinavia in early March and sail to the Canaries. Traders expected this to contain low sulphur fuel oil.
High sulphur fuel oil swaps headed down to around $81/$82 in March.
Gas oil was weaker with futures, but continued to attract good buying interest for fob material that can be worked out of region, while cif cargoes were seen as less desirable.

Russian premiums held up around cif high quotes +$1-2 because of tightness in the first decade of March. FOD spec was also attracting good premiums with material heard offered at fob high quotes +$4, although buyers were a couple of dollars off this.
